data.revised_prompt: The top-view quadcopter blockout in <Picture 1>, featuring a central rounded-rectangular body, four diagonal arms, and four circular rotor discs, is <Subject 1>. The plain white background and overhead framing in <Picture 1> are <Subject 2>. The target image transforms <Subject 1> into an 8K photorealistic industrial design rendering of a finished cold-grey quadcopter while maintaining its exact layout on <Subject 2>. <Subject 1> is partially preserved; its top-down spatial placement, scale, stretched X-shaped proportions, arm span ratio, and rotor positions remain, while its flat grey geometric shapes change into detailed three-dimensional hardware components. <Subject 2> is partially preserved; the overhead camera angle and clean studio backdrop remain, while soft 5500K lighting introduces realistic contact shadows beneath the rendered aircraft. The central fuselage of <Subject 1> becomes a streamlined carbon-fiber shell with sharp 60-degree beveled edges, an anodized aluminum honeycomb grille venting across the mid-section, and a flush-mounted GPS antenna integrated into the top surface. A glowing blue LED light band traces the perimeter of the fuselage. The four diagonal arms become foldable carbon-fiber booms connected to the body via metallic modular quick-release hinges. At the tips of the arms, the dark circular hubs transform into reinforced cylindrical motor covers with machined cooling fins, topped by translucent ABS propeller blades coated in a sleek nano-finish that occupy the original rotor disc footprints. Soft overhead illumination casts crisp, high-contrast shadows directly onto the white surface below.
